report.source_text: During the subsequent 9 months, visual acuity deteriorated considerably to a Snellen fraction of less than 20/200 on the right side and 25/100 on the left side. Concomitant bilateral cataracts and significant atrophy of the optic nerve (right>left) were documented. Bilateral cataract surgery was performed in a private practice without any amelioration of visual acuity. A tumour or inflammatory alterations of the optic nerve were ruled out by a brain MRI. A genetic panel for >100 genes related to hereditary optic atrophy including Leber’s hereditary optic neuropathy was also unrevealing.

report.source_text: One year later, the patient presented again at a neurological private practice due to further progression of his ataxia. Furthermore, a prominent relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD) was found. A repeated MRI scan showed regression of the formerly described herniated disc without any signs of myelopathy. Laboratory rheumatological screening (antineuronal antibodies) and tumour markers were unremarkable again. Electrophysiological testing did not show any clear evidence for the presence of a polyneuropathy.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A married carpenter in his 60s initially presented with diplopia attributed to presumed congenital left IVth cranial nerve paresis. Eight months later, neurological progression included left VIth cranial nerve palsy, pelvic pain radiating to the right leg, urge incontinence, symptoms of sensory polyneuropathy, decreased deep tendon reflexes, reduced vibration sense, and unsteady gait. Visual deterioration with bilateral optic nerve atrophy and cataracts ensued, with brain MRI and genetic testing excluding tumors and hereditary optic neuropathies. Rheumatological screening and tumor markers were negative, along with electrophysiology not clearly showing polyneuropathy. The patient later disclosed a prior syphilis infection 30 years earlier, likely insufficiently treated. Despite pending direct serological and CSF laboratory data in the disclosed information, the eventual diagnosis of tabes dorsalis was established based on clinical progression, history, and laboratory results referenced but not excerpted in the reports.
